h:
The Book of Enoch stands in the Ethiopian canon of Scripture, and Jude quotes it by name. Near its end, in chapters 93 and 91, sits a short prophecy called “the Apocalypse of Weeks.”

The setting is a father’s last instruction to his sons. Enoch sends for them through Methuselah.

“And now, my son Methuselah, call to me all thy brothers and gather together to me all the sons of thy mother; for the word calls me, and the spirit is poured out upon me, that I may show you everything that shall befall you for ever.” - 1 Enoch 91:1

Then he reads to them from the books and divides the course of the world into ten weeks. He places his own birth in the first.

The first six weeks run over ground that Genesis and Kings also cover. The seventh describes an apostate generation. The last three carry judgment to the oppressors, to the whole earth, and to the angels, and they end in a new heaven.

Enoch names no man in any of them. This essay lays his weeks beside Scripture and lets the two be seen together. It begins with the manuscript, because part of this prophecy came out of the Judean desert.

A Scroll from the Judean Desert

The complete Book of Enoch survives in Ge’ez, kept by the Ethiopian Church.

Among the Dead Sea Scrolls found near Qumran were copies of Enoch in Aramaic. One of them, 4Q212, carries portions of the ten weeks. It was written before the birth of Christ. The leather is torn: weeks three to six are gone, and weeks two and seven survive in pieces. The caves held a whole desert archive, and Enoch was in it.

The scroll settles the order. In the Ethiopic copies the first seven weeks stand in chapter 93 and the last three stand earlier, in chapter 91. In 4Q212 the seventh week runs straight into the eighth. So the weeks are read here as the scroll has them: chapter 93, then chapter 91.

From the First Man to the Burning House

Enoch begins with himself.

“I was born the seventh in the first week, while judgement and righteousness still endured.” - 1 Enoch 93:3

He counts himself the seventh and marks his week by one thing: righteousness still stood. Jude 1:14 gives him the same count: “Enoch, the seventh from Adam.”

The second week goes dark.

“And after me there shall arise in the second week great wickedness, and deceit shall have sprung up; and in it there shall be the first end. And in it a man shall be saved; and after it is ended unrighteousness shall grow up, And a law shall be made for the sinners.” - 1 Enoch 93:4

Great wickedness. A first end. One man saved. Enoch gives no name. Genesis tells of an earth gone to ruin and one man who found favor.

“But the earth was corrupted before God, and the earth was filled with iniquity.” - Genesis 6:11

“But Noe found grace before the Lord God.” - Genesis 6:8

Read Enoch’s last two lines again. After the end, unrighteousness grows up a second time. The end does not finish it. Genesis 6 is walked line by line in Who Were the Sons of God?

The third week turns on one man.

“And after that in the third week at its close a man shall be elected as the plant of righteous judgement, and his posterity shall become the plant of righteousness for evermore.” - 1 Enoch 93:5

A man chosen, and a promise that runs to his seed. Genesis has such a man.

“And I will make thee a great nation, and I will bless thee and magnify thy name, and thou shalt be blessed. And I will bless those that bless thee, and curse those that curse thee, and in thee shall all the tribes of the earth be blessed.” - Genesis 12:2-3

Enoch calls him a plant. A root in soil. The word comes back twice: as “the chosen root” in the sixth week, and as “the eternal plant of righteousness” in the seventh.

The fourth week brings a law.

“And after that in the fourth week, at its close, visions of the holy and righteous shall be seen, and a law for all generations and an enclosure shall be made for them.” - 1 Enoch 93:6

Visions, a law for all generations, a wall around a people. Exodus has a people brought to a mountain and bound by covenant.

“And now if ye will indeed hear my voice, and keep my covenant, ye shall be to me a peculiar people above all nations; for the whole earth is mine. And ye shall be to me a royal priesthood and a holy nation.” - Exodus 19:5-6

The fifth week brings a building.

“And after that in the fifth week, at its close, the house of glory and dominion shall be built for ever.” - 1 Enoch 93:7

In 3 Kingdoms a house is finished and the ark is carried into its inner room.

“And it came to pass when the priests departed out of the holy place, that the cloud filled the house. And the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, because the glory of the Lord filled the house.” - 3 Kingdoms 8:10-11

Then the sixth week.

“And after that in the sixth week all who live in it shall be blinded, and the hearts of all of them shall godlessly forsake wisdom. And in it a man shall ascend; and at its close the house of dominion shall be burnt with fire, and the whole race of the chosen root shall be dispersed.” - 1 Enoch 93:8

Four things in one week. Blindness. A man going up. The house burned. The root scattered.

4 Kingdoms holds a man going up. Elijah.

“And it came to pass as they were going, they went on talking; and, behold, a chariot of fire, and horses of fire, and it separated between them both; and Eliu was taken up in a whirlwind as it were into heaven.” - 4 Kingdoms 2:11

It holds a house burning.

“And he burnt the house of the Lord, and the king’s house, and all the houses of Jerusalem, even every house did the captain of the guard burn.” - 4 Kingdoms 25:9

And it closes the account in one line: “So Juda was carried away from his land,” 4 Kingdoms 25:21.

In Kings the ascent and the fire stand generations apart. Enoch holds both inside a single week.

Lay the six in a row. The first generations. A destruction with one man saved. One man chosen. A law. A house built. A house burned and a people scattered. Genesis through 4 Kingdoms runs in the same order.

Where the Landmarks Stop

“And after that in the seventh week shall an apostate generation arise, and many shall be its deeds, and all its deeds shall be apostate.” - 1 Enoch 93:9

No house. No man. No event. Only a generation and what it did. It turned.

Enoch fixes one thing about it: its place. It comes after the fire and the scattering. He gives it no date and no length. He gives what comes at its close.

“And at its close shall be elected
The elect righteous of the eternal plant of righteousness, to receive sevenfold instruction concerning all His creation.” - 1 Enoch 93:10

Out of the plant a remnant is chosen. They are taught. The measure is sevenfold. The subject is all His creation. The verse does not open the instruction any further.

Enoch does say where his own knowledge came from.

“According to that which appeared to me in the heavenly vision, and which I have known through the word of the holy angels, and have learnt from the heavenly tablets.” - 1 Enoch 93:2

His book is full of it: the courses of the sun and moon, the deeds of the Watchers, the sentence on the wicked.

Apostasy. Then instruction. Then the sword.

The Sword Climbs to Heaven

“And after that there shall be another, the eighth week, that of righteousness,
And a sword shall be given to it that a righteous judgement may be executed on the oppressors, and sinners shall be delivered into the hands of the righteous.” - 1 Enoch 91:12

“And at its close they shall acquire houses through their righteousness,
And a house shall be built for the Great King in glory for evermore, and all mankind shall look to the path of uprightness.” - 1 Enoch 91:13-14

A sword. Houses. Then a house.

It is the second house in the ten weeks. The first was built in the fifth week and burned in the sixth. Of this one Enoch says “in glory for evermore,” and no fire is written against it.

The reach widens too. Weeks three to six follow one man and his seed. Here it is all mankind. The prophet Isaiah saw a house and a road like it.

“For in the last days the mountain of the Lord shall be glorious, and the house of God shall be on the top of the mountains, and it shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall come to it.” - Isaiah 2:2

The ninth week takes the judgment further.

“And after that, in the ninth week, the righteous judgement shall be revealed to the whole world, and all the works of the godless shall vanish from all the earth, and the world shall be written down for destruction.” - 1 Enoch 91:14

And the tenth takes it higher.

“And after this, in the tenth week in the seventh part, there shall be the great eternal judgement, in which He will execute vengeance amongst the angels.” - 1 Enoch 91:15

Oppressors. The whole world. The angels. The judgment climbs week by week. Jude writes of angels held for a day like this.

“And the angels not having kept their domain, but having abandoned their own dwelling, He has kept in eternal chains under gloomy darkness unto the judgment of the great day.” - Jude 1:6

Then heaven itself gives way.

“And the first heaven shall depart and pass away, and a new heaven shall appear, and all the powers of the heavens shall give sevenfold light.” - 1 Enoch 91:16

Sevenfold, a second time. Sevenfold instruction at the close of the seventh week. Sevenfold light in the tenth.

John writes of a first heaven passing as well.

“And I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth passed away, and the sea is no more.” - Revelation 21:1

He records a sentence on the deceiver: “And the devil, the one deceiving them, was cast into the lake of fire and of sulfur,” Revelation 20:10. And he records what is left afterward.

“‘And He will wipe away every tear from their eyes,’ and death will be no more, nor mourning nor crying nor pain; they will be no more, because the first things passed away.” - Revelation 21:4

The two count differently. Enoch counts weeks. John is shown seals, trumpets, and bowls. Look at where each of them ends.

The Judge the Weeks Do Not Name

The ten weeks name no Messiah. They say only that “He will execute” the judgment.

Another part of the same book speaks of a judge.

“And he sat on the throne of his glory,
And the sum of judgement was given unto the Son of Man, and he caused the sinners to pass away and be destroyed from off the face of the earth, and those who have led the world astray.” - 1 Enoch 69:27

The Gospels speak this way.

“And when the Son of Man comes in His glory, and all the angels with Him, then He will sit upon the throne of His glory.” - Matthew 25:31

“And He gave Him authority to do judgment, because He is the Son of Man.” - John 5:27

The same title. The same throne of glory. Judgment given into his hand. Enoch does not stitch these two parts of his book together. They lie in the same book, and the Gospels use the same words.

Jude reaches into that book by name.

“And Enoch, the seventh from Adam, also prophesied as to these, saying: ‘Behold, the Lord came amidst myriads of His holy ones, to do judgment against all, and to convict all the ungodly concerning all their works of ungodliness that they did in an ungodly way, and concerning all the harsh things that ungodly sinners spoke against Him.’” - Jude 1:14-15

“And behold! He cometh with ten thousands of His holy ones to execute judgement upon all, and to destroy all the ungodly: and to convict all flesh of all the works of their ungodliness which they have ungodly committed, and of all the hard things which ungodly sinners have spoken against Him.” - 1 Enoch 1:9

Jude says Enoch prophesied. The words he gives stand in the first chapter of the book that holds the ten weeks. Tertullian, writing around the year 200, put it in one line in On the Apparel of Women: “Enoch possesses a testimony in the Apostle Jude.” The Ethiopian Church holds the whole book in its canon. What became of it elsewhere is traced in The Self-Proving Prophecy.

So the weeks stand. Six of them lie along the road from Genesis to the exile. The seventh has no landmark. The last three rise from the oppressors to the angels.

And Enoch leaves questions shut. Which generation is the seventh? What is the sevenfold instruction? When is the sword given? What is the house of the Great King? Where in the ten weeks does the Son of Man come?

He does not leave the end shut.

“And after that there will be many weeks without number for ever, and all shall be in goodness and righteousness, and sin shall no more be mentioned for ever.” - 1 Enoch 91:17

The counting stops.

Weeks without number. Sin not so much as named.
